headline: Offseason build: needs, additions, and the path to next season
dek: Last game on the tape, where the Chiefs stand, and the plan for who's next.
videoHook: Let's get into it — KC: the last game, where we stand, and Denver Broncos.
theEdge: Model/market read: the model gives KC 58.5%; Vegas has it KC -3; Polymarket prices the Chiefs at 6.2% to win it all.

storyline.lede: The roster story keeps moving. Here's where the Chiefs stand, what still needs answering, and how the pieces point toward the season ahead.
body: This edition runs the weekly desk in order: last game, current state, next opponent.

The last look at Seattle Seahawks is now in the book. ESPN had KC at 353 total yards against 266 for the opponent; turnovers KC 1 / opp 1; KC third downs 9-17. Treat it as a teaching tape: who earned snaps, who lost them, and which calls survived contact.
Offseason work is still about flipping 6-11 from 2025. Coming off T KC 9–9 vs. Seattle Seahawks. The opener is the finish line for every addition.

Denver Broncos is the first real stress test of the new identity. If the run and the nickel are not ready, Denver Broncos will make Kansas City play the 2025 game. For context, the model gives KC 58.5%; Vegas has it KC -3; Polymarket prices the Chiefs at 6.2% to win it all.

xsandos.title: Inside zone — stay on schedule
xsandos.why: Early-down efficiency keeps the play-action and boot menu honest and the offense out of obvious passing downs — where opponents want it.
xsandos.coaching: One cut, downhill — let the double-teams move the line and take the four yards every time.

xsandos.title: Under-center boot — the early-down answer
xsandos.situation: 1st & 10 off a run look vs. Denver Broncos
xsandos.why: Moves the launch point away from the rush and gives a defined half-field read — the cheapest explosive in the menu once the run game has landed.
xsandos.coaching: The fake has to match the run action on tape or the backside end never bites.

xsandos.title: 4 verticals vs. Cover 3
xsandos.why: Stretches the deep zones and forces the safety to choose — a staple answer when the defense sits back.
xsandos.coaching: Bend the seams to the hash and read the safety's leverage.

xsandos.title: Mesh vs. man
xsandos.why: Rub-heavy crossers beat man coverage and give a clean, quick answer with an RB checkdown as the outlet.
xsandos.coaching: Set the mesh depth tight so the pick is legal and natural.

xsandos.title: Simulated pressure on the money down
xsandos.why: Five-man picture, four-man rush: force the hot throw into a capped window without selling out the coverage behind it.
xsandos.coaching: The dropper must land in the throwing lane the protection leaves open — that's where the hot ball goes.

xsandos.title: Spagnuolo Cover-2 shell
xsandos.situation: Protect a lead / obvious passing down
xsandos.why: Takes the top off, rallies to tackle, and dares the offense to be patient — the situational change-up.
xsandos.coaching: Sink the corners, funnel everything to the deep halves.
